title: CLAUDE.md
text: Upstream stacks BMF vintages mixed source dtypes writes result almost every column string, design — explicit typing failed across vintage seam. Concretely: Numeric-looking columns (asset_amount, income_amount, revenue_amount, geo_score, geo_distance, …) arrive character. Cast .numeric() consumer. Code columns (subsection_code, classification_code, foundation_code, affiliation_code, accounting_period, asset_code, income_code, filing_requirement_code, org_addr_zip5, org_addr_zip4, geo_postal, activity_code, ruling_date_ym_str, tax_period_ym_str, …) arrive character. Treat IDs; cast needed. Boolean-looking columns (group_exemption_is_member, org_addr_is_po_box, org_addr_is_rural_route, org_addr_has_special_chars, org_addr_is_missing, org_addr_missing_number, org_addr_state_invalid, ruling_date_is_missing, tax_period_is_missing, in_care_of_name_provided) arrive character (“True”/“False”). Use nccs_as_indicator() coerce — exactly case helper built , “re-cleaning package output” rule apply indicator/financial coercion . Date columns (ruling_date, tax_period_ymd) arrive character YYYY-MM-DD form. Cast .Date(). Columns keep proper types: geo_lat/geo_lon (double), geo_is_geocoded (logical), first_year_in_bmf / last_year_in_bmf (integer), bmf_vintages_observed (double). bundled data dictionary (bmf_dictionary) records actual -disk type column, source truth — list, illustrative.

title: CLAUDE.md
text: R/nccs_read.R — Core function. Reads BMF parquet S3 optional predicate-pushdown filters (state, county, NTEE subsector, exempt org type). Supports column selection lazy Arrow queries. R/nccs_core_url.R, R/nccs_read_core.R, R/nccs_core_columns.R, R/nccs_core_coverage.R — CORE Series (Form 990 filings) surface. Three tiers (merged / soi / legacy) s3://nccsdata/processed{,_legacy,_merged}/core/{tax_year}/{form}/. partition parquet + CSV data file parquet + CSV column dictionary. nccs_read_core() accepts vector tax_year stacks requested partitions one Arrow dataset; downloading anything cache reports total transfer size , confirm = interactive(), prompts. Partitions don’t exist upstream dropped message() rather erroring, year range straddles gap still works. Tier coverage notes (legacy: 990 / 990ez; SOI: 2017-2019 990pf partitions present contain backfilled tax-year rows 2020+ extracts — sparse, original calendar-year publication; merged: dedup keeps first (ein, tax_period)) documented nccs_core_url() validated .validate_core_partition(). R/nccs_summary.R — Grouped count summaries collected data. R/nccs_catalog.R — Lists valid filter values (offline, network needed). Supports labels = TRUE return code + description tibble fields backed bundled lookup. R/nccs_dictionary.R — Returns BMF data dictionary tibble optional grep filtering. Also documents bmf_dictionary dataset. R/nccs_normalize_ein.R — Coerces arbitrary EIN inputs canonical XX-XXXXXXX form. Pure, base-R . R/nccs_as_indicator.R — Coerces IRS binary-indicator columns logical, yn efile schemes vintage-specific encodings. R/nccs_deflate.R + R/cpi_u.R — Real-dollar conversion CORE financial columns. nccs_deflate(amount, year, base_year) uses bundled annual CPI-U series (FRED CPIAUCNS, 1913-present, refreshed via data-raw/build_cpi.R). one opinionated analytic helper package — canonical financial ratios (operating margin, program-expense ratio, etc.) deliberately bundled definitions vary analyst.

title: Getting Started with nccsdata
text: nccsdata package provides access nonprofit organization data National Center Charitable Statistics (NCCS). reads IRS Business Master File (BMF) data stored parquet files public S3 bucket, support efficient filtering state, county, NTEE subsector, exempt organization type. package requires API keys authentication — data publicly accessible.

title: Getting Started with nccsdata
text: querying data, can explore 97 available columns using nccs_dictionary():
code: library(nccsdata)  # See all available columns nccs_dictionary()  # Find geocoding-related columns nccs_dictionary("geo")  # Find NTEE classification columns nccs_dictionary("ntee")

title: Getting Started with nccsdata
text: Use nccs_catalog() see valid values filter querying:
code: # NTEE v2 subsector codes nccs_catalog("ntee_subsector") #> [1] "ART" "EDU" "ENV" "HEL" "HMS" "HOS" "IFA" "MMB" "PSB" "REL" "UNI" "UNU"  # State and territory codes nccs_catalog("state")  # Exempt organization types (e.g., 501(c)(3), 501(c)(4), etc.) nccs_catalog("exempt_org_type")

title: Getting Started with nccsdata
text: core function nccs_read(), reads BMF data S3 predicate-pushdown filtering efficient reads.

title: Getting Started with nccsdata
code: # All nonprofits in Pennsylvania pa <- nccs_read(state = "PA") nrow(pa)

title: Getting Started with nccsdata
code: # Nonprofits in specific Pennsylvania counties nepa <- nccs_read(   state = "PA",   county = c("Lackawanna County", "Luzerne County", "Wayne County") ) nrow(nepa)

title: Getting Started with nccsdata
code: # Arts organizations in Pennsylvania pa_arts <- nccs_read(state = "PA", ntee_subsector = "ART") nrow(pa_arts)

title: Getting Started with nccsdata
text: org_type argument bundles common 501(c)(3) cuts don’t manage subsection_code foundation_code hand: Pass org_type = "501c3" keep public charities private foundations, "" (default) skip filter entirely.
code: # All 501(c)(3) public charities pc <- nccs_read(org_type = "public_charity")  # California private foundations ca_pf <- nccs_read(state = "CA", org_type = "private_foundation")  # Everything that is not a 501(c)(3) non_c3 <- nccs_read(org_type = "non_501c3")

title: Getting Started with nccsdata
text: BMF parquet file contains 97 columns 400 MB. default, nccs_read() returns curated subset commonly needed columns. can customize :
code: # Specify exact columns (minimizes download size) pa_slim <- nccs_read(   state = "PA",   columns = c("ein", "org_name_display", "geo_county", "nteev2_subsector") ) names(pa_slim)  # Get all 97 columns (slower) pa_full <- nccs_read(state = "PA", columns = "all")

title: Getting Started with nccsdata
text: Set collect = FALSE get lazy Arrow query instead tibble. useful building custom dplyr chains collecting:
code: library(dplyr)  query <- nccs_read(state = "PA", collect = FALSE)  # Add custom filters and transformations result <- query |>   filter(geo_county == "Lackawanna County") |>   select(ein, org_name_display, nteev2_subsector) |>   collect()

title: Getting Started with nccsdata
text: published BMF parquet stores columns character (upstream pipeline stacks vintages writes strings). default nccs_read() coerces well-known columns natural R types collected tibble: asset_amount, income_amount, revenue_amount, geo_score, geo_distance → numeric. ruling_date, tax_period_ymd → Date. org_addr_is_*, ruling_date_is_missing, tax_period_is_missing group_exemption_is_member style flags → logical (via nccs_as_indicator()). ID-like codes (subsection_code, classification_code, ZIPs, NTEE codes) stay character — ’re identifiers, numbers. Pass coerce = FALSE skip coercion get every column exactly published.

title: Getting Started with nccsdata
text: master BMF parquet hundreds MB. nccs_read() caches tools::R_user_dir("nccsdata", "cache") first use reuses local copy subsequent calls (session across sessions). cached file refreshed automatically ’s older cache_max_age days (30 default, matching upstream monthly rebuild cadence). Disable cache = FALSE, force refresh:
code: nccs_cache_dir() nccs_cache_clear()

title: Getting Started with nccsdata
text: nccs_read() reads rolling geocoded master, upstream pipeline rebuilds every month. analyses need specific dated snapshot (papers, dashboards, regulatory work), use nccs_vintage_url() get S3 URI month, read CSV directly: Vintage snapshots geocoded — carry raw Form 990 address columns instead master’s geo_* columns. Schemas also drift across vintages across legacy seam (pre-modern vintages live bmf-legacy path; pass legacy = TRUE nccs_vintage_url()). Always inspect matching data dictionary filtering joining.
code: uri  <- nccs_vintage_url("2023_07") dict <- arrow::read_csv_arrow(   nccs_vintage_url("2023_07", kind = "dictionary") ) bmf_2023_07 <- arrow::read_csv_arrow(uri)

title: Getting Started with nccsdata
text: BMF one row per registered organization. work one row per filing, use CORE Series — Form 990 filings harmonized single schema across vintages. Three tiers published: "merged" (canonical, default): legacy + SOI-current merged (ein, tax_period). One row per (ein, tax_period), 1987-2024, forms 990combined 990pf. Deduplicated — keeps first occurrence per key. "soi": IRS SOI annual extracts, harmonized. 2012-2024, forms 990, 990ez, 990pf, 990combined. Carries is_amendment flag need separate originals revisions. "legacy": NCCS legacy CORE files, harmonized. 1987-2011, forms 990combined 990pf. multi-year analyses, pass vector tax_year. function stacks requested partitions one Arrow dataset (filters column projection still push across ) , interactive session, reports total download size fetching partitions doesn’t already cached. nccs_core_coverage() returns row counts every published partition tier — useful sanity checks quickly spotting coverage gaps (e.g. SOI’s missing 2017-2019 990pf partitions).
code: # Inspect a partition's columns before reading dict <- nccs_core_columns("merged", 2020, "990combined") head(dict[, c("harmonized_name", "data_type", "description")])  # Read one partition with column projection df <- nccs_read_core(   tier     = "merged",   tax_year = 2020,   form     = "990combined",   columns  = c("ein", "tax_period", "total_revenue", "total_expenses") )  # Or build a lazy query for custom filters nccs_read_core("merged", 2020, "990combined", collect = FALSE) |>   dplyr::filter(subsection_cd == 3) |>   dplyr::select(ein, tax_period, total_revenue) |>   dplyr::collect() panel <- nccs_read_core(   tier     = "merged",   tax_year = 2015:2022,   form     = "990combined",   columns  = c("ein", "tax_period", "total_revenue", "total_expenses") )

title: Getting Started with nccsdata
text: nccs_summary() produces grouped count summaries:
code: pa <- nccs_read(state = "PA")  # Total count nccs_summary(pa)  # Count by county nccs_summary(pa, group_by = "geo_county")  # Count by county and NTEE subsector nccs_summary(pa, group_by = c("geo_county", "nteev2_subsector"))

title: Getting Started with nccsdata
text: Write summary results CSV:
code: pa <- nccs_read(   state = "PA",   county = c("Lackawanna County", "Luzerne County", "Wayne County") )  nccs_summary(   pa,   group_by = c("geo_county", "nteev2_subsector"),   output_csv = "nepa_nonprofit_counts.csv" )

title: Spatial Joins with TIGER/Line Geographies
text: nccs_read() exposes coarsest geographic filters predicate-pushdown cheaply BMF parquet: state county. anything finer — congressional districts, Census tracts, block groups, ZCTAs, metropolitan statistical areas — every BMF row carries precise geocoded point (geo_lat, geo_lon), spatial join accurate flexible filtering mailing address. vignette shows take BMF rows nccs_read() join TIGER/Line geographies pulled tigris package, using sf spatial operation. None packages imported nccsdata — install need .
code: install.packages(c("tigris", "sf"))

what: Why not filter on city or ZIP?
title: Spatial Joins with TIGER/Line Geographies
text: BMF’s city ZIP fields come organization’s mailing address, operating location, ZIP codes USPS delivery routes rather analytical geographies. Joining geo_lat / geo_lon TIGER polygons gives actual containing geography lets swap one geography another (tracts vs. districts vs. places) without re-querying BMF.

title: Spatial Joins with TIGER/Line Geographies
text: recipe regardless target geography: Pull BMF rows nccs_read(). Convert lat/lon columns sf point layer WGS84 (EPSG:4326). Pull TIGER polygon layer target geography. Reproject common CRS sf::st_join().
code: library(nccsdata) library(dplyr) library(sf) library(tigris)  options(tigris_use_cache = TRUE)

title: Spatial Joins with TIGER/Line Geographies
text: Attach 119th Congress district every nonprofit Pennsylvania. pa_with_cd sf object — drop geometry sf::st_drop_geometry() need tabular result.
code: pa <- nccs_read(state = "PA") |>   filter(!is.na(geo_lat), !is.na(geo_lon))  pa_sf <- st_as_sf(pa, coords = c("geo_lon", "geo_lat"), crs = 4326)  cd <- congressional_districts(state = "PA", cb = TRUE, year = 2024) |>   st_transform(4326)  pa_with_cd <- st_join(pa_sf, cd["CD119FP"])

title: Spatial Joins with TIGER/Line Geographies
text: Roll nonprofits tract level Allegheny County, PA.
code: ac <- nccs_read(state = "PA", county = "Allegheny County") |>   filter(!is.na(geo_lat), !is.na(geo_lon)) |>   st_as_sf(coords = c("geo_lon", "geo_lat"), crs = 4326)  tracts_ac <- tracts(state = "PA", county = "Allegheny", year = 2023) |>   st_transform(4326)  ac_with_tract <- st_join(ac, tracts_ac["GEOID"])  orgs_per_tract <- ac_with_tract |>   st_drop_geometry() |>   count(GEOID, name = "n_orgs") |>   arrange(desc(n_orgs))

what: Example 3 — ZCTAs (the right way to use ZIPs)
title: Spatial Joins with TIGER/Line Geographies
text: downstream question really ZIP-based, use Census ZCTAs rather BMF’s mailing ZIP — ’re stable polygons can join ACS Census tabulations. ZCTAs 2020 onward, tigris::zctas() serves full national layer — state argument retired Census Bureau stopped publishing state-level ZCTA files. Pull national (caches) let spatial join restrict California.
code: ca <- nccs_read(state = "CA") |>   filter(!is.na(geo_lat), !is.na(geo_lon)) |>   st_as_sf(coords = c("geo_lon", "geo_lat"), crs = 4326)  zcta <- zctas(year = 2020) |>   st_transform(4326)  ca_with_zcta <- st_join(ca, zcta["ZCTA5CE20"])

title: Spatial Joins with TIGER/Line Geographies
text: tigris caches downloaded shapefiles user’s R cache directory tigris_use_cache = TRUE — large pulls (every U.S. tract) download reuse subsequent calls. Choose matching TIGER vintage joining ACS decennial Census data, otherwise GEOIDs may align across years. Points falling outside TIGER layer (foreign addresses, unmatched geocodes) yield NA joined columns — filter tabulation needed.

title: Working with the CORE Series (Form 990 filings)
text: NCCS CORE Series set harmonized Form 990 filings, partitioned (tax_year, form) published parquet S3. row one filing — financial totals, organization identifiers, NTEE codes, exemption status, — already cleaned column-aligned across vintages upstream pipeline. Background column-level documentation live NCCS site: CORE datasets overview CORE data catalog package exposes four CORE helpers — nccs_core_url(), nccs_read_core(), nccs_core_columns(), nccs_core_coverage() — vignette shows workflows ’re designed .

title: Working with the CORE Series (Form 990 filings)
text: CORE published three tiers, different harmonization underlying IRS source data: rough decision tree: Cross-year panel, current era → merged. Need separate originals amendments, need 990 / 990ez split → soi. Pre-2012 → legacy (merged, now includes years). merged tier carries two extra columns — source_pipeline has_legacy_augment — let trace row back upstream source need . caveat worth knowing: SOI 990pf 2017-2019 technically present, contains backfilled tax-year rows 2020+ calendar-year extracts (original calendar-year publication exists). Row counts tiny (≈665, 3.3k, 100k). merged tier folds cleanly.

title: Working with the CORE Series (Form 990 filings)
text: Every partition publishes column dictionary. Use nccs_core_columns() see ’s available without downloading filings parquet . nccs_core_url() returns canonical S3 URL partition dictionary file want inspect outside R:
code: library(nccsdata) library(dplyr)  dict <- nccs_core_columns("merged", 2020, "990combined") head(dict[, c("harmonized_name", "data_type", "description")]) nccs_core_url("merged", 2020, "990combined") nccs_core_url("soi", 2020, "990", kind = "dictionary")

title: Working with the CORE Series (Form 990 filings)
text: nccs_read_core() reads single (tier, tax_year, form) partition column projection (requested columns leave S3) local caching default. larger queries, drop collect = FALSE keep result Arrow query push filters / aggregations parquet:
code: df <- nccs_read_core(   tier     = "merged",   tax_year = 2020,   form     = "990combined",   columns  = c("ein", "tax_period", "total_revenue",                "total_expenses", "total_assets_eoy") ) nccs_read_core("merged", 2020, "990combined", collect = FALSE) |>   filter(subsection_cd == 3, total_revenue > 1e6) |>   select(ein, tax_period, total_revenue, total_expenses) |>   collect()

title: Working with the CORE Series (Form 990 filings)
text: Pass vector tax_year. function stacks requested partitions one Arrow dataset, filters column projection still push across . downloading anything isn’t already caching, function reports total transfer size (interactive sessions) prompts: Subsequent calls (tier, form, year) partition hit local cache instead S3. cache lives nccs_cache_dir() — see ?nccs_cache_clear need wipe . nccs_core_coverage() lists every published partition tier row counts, useful sanity check spotting small / backfilled partitions:
code: panel <- nccs_read_core(   tier     = "merged",   tax_year = 2015:2022,   form     = "990combined",   columns  = c("ein", "tax_period", "total_revenue",                "total_expenses", "total_assets_eoy") ) #> nccs_read_core: downloading 8 partition(s) (~3.4 GB) to local #> cache for years 2015, 2016, 2017, 2018, 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022. #> Continue? (Yes/no/cancel) nccs_core_coverage("soi") |>   filter(form == "990pf") |>   arrange(tax_year)

title: Working with the CORE Series (Form 990 filings)
text: Multi-year panels mix nominal dollars different years. comparing aggregating across years, deflate common base year nccs_deflate(), uses bundled annual CPI-U series (cpi_u): package deliberately stops deflation — canonical financial ratios (operating margin, program-expense ratio, fundraising efficiency, etc.) one-line mutate() calls whose definitions vary analyst, don’t ship opinionated wrappers.
code: panel_real <- panel |>   mutate(     total_revenue_2023  = nccs_deflate(as.numeric(total_revenue),                                        year = as.integer(substr(tax_period, 1, 4)),                                        base_year = 2023),     total_expenses_2023 = nccs_deflate(as.numeric(total_expenses),                                        year = as.integer(substr(tax_period, 1, 4)),                                        base_year = 2023)   )

what: Joining CORE filings to BMF metadata
title: Working with the CORE Series (Form 990 filings)
text: CORE rows include financial fields form-specific data, richer organizational metadata (NTEE codes, geocoded location, subsection classifications) lives BMF. two surfaces share ein canonical key. Bringing list EINs external CSV? Run nccs_normalize_ein() first match canonical form used CORE BMF:
code: # Pull 2022 filings from the merged CORE filings_2022 <- nccs_read_core(   tier     = "merged",   tax_year = 2022,   form     = "990combined",   columns  = c("ein", "tax_period", "total_revenue", "total_expenses") )  # Pull BMF rows for California arts orgs only — geo + NTEE come from BMF ca_arts <- nccs_read(   state           = "CA",   ntee_subsector  = "ART" ) |>   select(ein, organization_name, geo_county, nteev2_code,          exempt_organization_type)  # EIN is canonical XX-XXXXXXX in both surfaces — direct join ca_arts_2022 <- inner_join(ca_arts, filings_2022, by = "ein") external <- read.csv("my_orgs.csv") external$ein <- nccs_normalize_ein(external$ein)  filings <- inner_join(filings_2022, external, by = "ein")

title: Working with the CORE Series (Form 990 filings)
text: columns CORE parquet land character keep schemas stable across vintages — cast numeric date columns consumer (.numeric(), .Date()). Use nccs_as_indicator() IRS Yes/fields. nccs_core_coverage() issues one HTTP request per partition (footer metadata , full scan) typically takes 10-60 seconds per tier. CORE catalog nccs.urban.org/nccs/catalogs/catalog-core.html canonical browseable reference column definitions across years forms.

what: Access and Analyze NCCS Nonprofit Data
title: Access and Analyze NCCS Nonprofit Data
text: nccsdata provides tools download, filter, analyze nonprofit organization data National Center Charitable Statistics (NCCS). reads IRS Business Master File (BMF) data stored parquet files public S3 bucket, support predicate-pushdown filtering state, county, NTEE subsector, exempt organization type. Note: version 2.0.0, ground-rewrite package. v1 API (get_data(), preview_sample(), parse_ntee()) replaced. See migration section .

title: Access and Analyze NCCS Nonprofit Data
text: Install development version GitHub:
code: # install.packages("devtools") devtools::install_github("UrbanInstitute/nccsdata")

title: Access and Analyze NCCS Nonprofit Data
text: nccs_read() downloads BMF data S3 optional filters. Filtering happens Arrow level via predicate pushdown, matching rows read memory.
code: library(nccsdata)  # All Pennsylvania nonprofits (default columns) pa <- nccs_read(state = "PA")  # Arts nonprofits in New York ny_arts <- nccs_read(state = "NY", ntee_subsector = "ART")  # Select specific columns pa_slim <- nccs_read(   state = "PA",   columns = c("ein", "org_name_display", "geo_county", "income_amount") )  # Lazy query for custom dplyr pipelines query <- nccs_read(state = "PA", collect = FALSE) result <- query |>   dplyr::filter(geo_county == "Lackawanna County") |>   dplyr::collect()

title: Access and Analyze NCCS Nonprofit Data
text: nccs_summary() produces grouped count summaries collected data frame.
code: pa <- nccs_read(state = "PA")  # Total count nccs_summary(pa)  # Count by county nccs_summary(pa, group_by = "geo_county")  # Count by county and subsector, export to CSV nccs_summary(pa, group_by = c("geo_county", "nteev2_subsector"),              output_csv = "pa_counts.csv")

title: Access and Analyze NCCS Nonprofit Data
text: nccs_catalog() lists valid values nccs_read() filters without network calls.
code: nccs_catalog("state") nccs_catalog("ntee_subsector") nccs_catalog("exempt_org_type")  # Pass `labels = TRUE` for a code + description tibble, sourced from the # bundled BMF lookup tables. nccs_catalog("ntee_subsector", labels = TRUE) nccs_catalog("foundation_code", labels = TRUE)

title: Access and Analyze NCCS Nonprofit Data
text: BMF returned nccs_read() already normalized upstream, two helpers exposed users joining external CSVs API responses :
code: # Coerce EINs in any format to canonical XX-XXXXXXX nccs_normalize_ein(c("123456789", "12-3456789", 1234567)) #> [1] "12-3456789" "12-3456789" "00-1234567"  # Coerce IRS binary-indicator columns to logical nccs_as_indicator(c("Y", "N", "1", "2")) #> [1]  TRUE FALSE  TRUE FALSE  # e-file indicator accepts E/P (2015, 2018+) and Y/N (2016-2017) nccs_as_indicator(c("E", "P", "Y", "N"), scheme = "efile")

title: Access and Analyze NCCS Nonprofit Data

code: # All columns nccs_dictionary()  # Find geocoding-related columns nccs_dictionary("geo")  # Find NTEE-related columns nccs_dictionary("ntee")

what: Coerce IRS Binary-Indicator Columns to Logical — nccs_as_indicator
title: Coerce IRS Binary-Indicator Columns to Logical — nccs_as_indicator
text: IRS Business Master File extracts encode binary fields using inconsistent tokens vary vintage. helper coerces column logical vector one two well-known schemes.

title: Coerce IRS Binary-Indicator Columns to Logical — nccs_as_indicator
code: nccs_as_indicator(x, scheme = c("yn", "efile"))

title: Coerce IRS Binary-Indicator Columns to Logical — nccs_as_indicator
text: x character, numeric, logical vector. scheme One `"yn"` (default) `"efile"`.

title: Coerce IRS Binary-Indicator Columns to Logical — nccs_as_indicator
text: logical vector length `x`.

title: Coerce IRS Binary-Indicator Columns to Logical — nccs_as_indicator
text: `"yn"` — general yes/indicator columns (often `_cd` suffix upstream data). TRUE:  `Y`, `y`, `1`, `T`, `TRUE`, `true`, `True` FALSE: `N`, `n`, `0`, `2`, `F`, `FALSE`, `false`, `False` Note `"2"` maps FALSE: IRS shifted binary fields 1 (= yes) / 2 (= ) encoding recent vintages (e.g. 2022/2023 990 columns). `"efile"` — IRS e-file indicator, whose accepted tokens vary filing year: 2015 990 / 990-EZ used `E` (electronic) / `P` (paper). 2016 2017 990 / 990-EZ switched `Y` / `N`. 2018 onwards returned `E` / `P`. three encodings accepted: TRUE:  `E`, `e`, `Y`, `y`, `1`, `T`, `TRUE`, `true`, `True` FALSE: `P`, `p`, `N`, `n`, `0`, `F`, `FALSE`, `false`, `False` Tokens outside accepted set become `NA`, single `warning()` lists distinct unknown values (one per element). `NA` input propagated silently. Pure base-R, side effects, -place mutation. Designed use external data user joining [nccs_read()] output — columns returned `nccs_read()` already cleaned upstream.

title: Coerce IRS Binary-Indicator Columns to Logical — nccs_as_indicator
code: nccs_as_indicator(c("Y", "N", "1", "2", NA)) #> [1]  TRUE FALSE  TRUE FALSE    NA # [1]  TRUE FALSE  TRUE FALSE    NA  nccs_as_indicator(c("E", "P", "Y", "N"), scheme = "efile") #> [1]  TRUE FALSE  TRUE FALSE # [1]  TRUE FALSE  TRUE FALSE

text: tier One `"merged"` (default, canonical), `"soi"`, `"legacy"`. See Description. tax_year Integer tax year. form Character form code: `"990"`, `"990ez"`, `"990pf"`, `"990combined"`. every form exists every tier — see Description. format One `"parquet"` (default) `"csv"`. kind One `"data"` (default) filings table `"dictionary"` per-partition column dictionary.

title: URL of an NCCS CORE Series Partition — nccs_core_url
text: single character HTTPS URL.

title: URL of an NCCS CORE Series Partition — nccs_core_url
text: `"merged"` (default, canonical) Legacy + SOI-current merged     `(ein, tax_period)` SOI precedence. One row per     `(ein, tax_period)`. Adds `source_pipeline`     `has_legacy_augment` columns. Tax years 1987-2024. Forms     `990combined`, `990pf`. **Deduplicated** — keeps first occurrence     per `(ein, tax_period)`; use `"soi"` `"legacy"` instead     need every original filing plus amendment. `"soi"` IRS SOI annual extracts, harmonized. Tax years     2012-2024. Forms `990`, `990ez`, `990pf`, `990combined`. Includes     `is_amendment` filtering originals vs revisions. 2024     partial year. `990pf` 2017-2019 present contain     backfilled tax-year rows 2020+ calendar-year extracts     (original calendar-year 2017-2019 PF SOI published); row     counts small (~665, 3.3k, 100k). provenance-aware     reads, use `"merged"` tier (carries `source_pipeline`     `has_legacy_augment`). `"legacy"` NCCS legacy CORE files, harmonized. Tax years     1987-2011. Forms `990combined`, `990pf`. amendment flag —     duplicates `(ein, tax_period)` exist     distinguished. `1993/990pf` ~11k rows. partition contains data file column dictionary, published parquet CSV. Prefer parquet — supports predicate pushdown column projection (see [nccs_read_core()]).

title: Convert Nominal Dollars to Real (Inflation-Adjusted) Dollars — nccs_deflate
text: amount Numeric vector nominal dollar amounts. year Integer vector years amounts denominated . Length 1 `length(amount)`. base_year Single integer. year whose dollars result expressed . Must present bundled series. cpi Optional override. two-column data frame `year` (integer) `cpi` (numeric); defaults bundled [cpi_u] table. Useful want use different deflator (e.g. PCE, GDP) custom snapshot CPI-U.

title: Convert Nominal Dollars to Real (Inflation-Adjusted) Dollars — nccs_deflate
text: Numeric vector length `amount`, `base_year`   dollars. `NA` input element whose year   series; single warning lists missing years.

title: Convert Nominal Dollars to Real (Inflation-Adjusted) Dollars — nccs_deflate
text: CORE Form 990 panels covering many years, deflating financial columns usually prerequisite cross-year comparison. helper thin wrapper around vector arithmetic — exists () bundle CPI lookup table users fetch , (b) standardize lookup behavior (warning --series years, NA propagation).

title: Convert Nominal Dollars to Real (Inflation-Adjusted) Dollars — nccs_deflate

what: Normalize EINs to Canonical IRS Format — nccs_normalize_ein
title: Normalize EINs to Canonical IRS Format — nccs_normalize_ein
text: Coerces vector Employer Identification Numbers (EINs) canonical IRS display format `XX-XXXXXXX` (10 characters, two digits, hyphen, seven digits). Useful users joining external data (CSV exports, spreadsheets, API responses) BMF returned [nccs_read()], whose `ein` column already normalized upstream.

title: Normalize EINs to Canonical IRS Format — nccs_normalize_ein
code: nccs_normalize_ein(x)

title: Normalize EINs to Canonical IRS Format — nccs_normalize_ein
Normalize EINs to Canonical IRS Format — nccs_normalize_ein
text: character vector length `x`, element either   `XX-XXXXXXX` form `NA_character_`.

title: Normalize EINs to Canonical IRS Format — nccs_normalize_ein
text: function strips non-digit characters, left-pads nine digits zeros (recover EINs lost leading zero numeric coercion), inserts hyphen position 3. Values reduced non-empty digit string nine fewer characters become `NA_character_`. Pure base-R, side effects, -place mutation.

title: Normalize EINs to Canonical IRS Format — nccs_normalize_ein
code: nccs_normalize_ein(c("123456789", "12-3456789", 123456789)) #> [1] "12-3456789" "12-3456789" "12-3456789" # All three become "12-3456789".  nccs_normalize_ein("1234567")       # leading zeros restored -> "00-1234567" #> [1] "00-1234567" nccs_normalize_ein(c("abc", NA))    # both become NA #> [1] NA NA

what: Read NCCS BMF Data from S3 — nccs_read
title: Read NCCS BMF Data from S3 — nccs_read
text: Reads NCCS Business Master File (BMF) stored parquet file public S3 bucket. Supports predicate-pushdown filtering state, county, NTEE classification (subsector, code, NTEEv2 code, major group), exempt organization type, financial size, BMF recency efficient reads.

title: Read NCCS BMF Data from S3 — nccs_read
code: nccs_read(   state = NULL,   county = NULL,   ntee_subsector = NULL,   ntee_major_group = NULL,   ntee_code = NULL,   nteev2_code = NULL,   exempt_org_type = NULL,   org_type = c("all", "501c3", "public_charity", "pc", "private_foundation", "pf",     "non_501c3"),   size_metric = c("revenue", "income", "asset"),   size_min = NULL,   size_max = NULL,   min_last_year = NULL,   cache = TRUE,   cache_max_age = 30L,   coerce = TRUE,   columns = NULL,   collect = TRUE )

title: Read NCCS BMF Data from S3 — nccs_read
text: state Character vector two-letter state abbreviations (e.g., `"PA"`, `c("PA", "NY")`). Filters `org_addr_state`. county Character vector county names (e.g., `"Lackawanna County"`). Filters `geo_county`. ntee_subsector Character vector NTEEv2 subsector values. Accepts either subsector codes (`"UNI"`, `"ART"`) human-readable names (`"Universities"`, `"Arts, Culture Humanities"`), matched case-insensitively. See [nccs_catalog()] valid values. Filters `nteev2_subsector`. ntee_major_group Character vector single-letter NTEE major groups (`""` `"Z"`). Filters `ntee_code_major_group`. See [nccs_catalog("ntee_major_group", labels = TRUE)] descriptions. ntee_code Character vector standardized 3-character NTEE codes (e.g., `"B40"`, `c("A20", "A23")`). Filters `ntee_code_clean`. validated — invalid codes just return rows. nteev2_code Character vector NTEEv2 3-character codes. Filters `nteev2_code`. validated. exempt_org_type Character vector exempt organization type descriptions. See [nccs_catalog()] valid values. Filters `exempt_organization_type`. org_type Convenience filter combines `subsection_code` `foundation_code` four common 501(c)(3) cuts plus complement. One : `""` (default) — filter. `"501c3"` — every 501(c)(3) organization     (`subsection_code == "3"`). `"public_charity"` / `"pc"` — 501(c)(3) public charities     (foundation codes three private-foundation     types). `"private_foundation"` / `"pf"` — 501(c)(3) private     foundations (`foundation_code` `"2"`, `"3"`, `"4"`). `"non_501c3"` — everything 501(c)(3). size_metric One `"revenue"`, `"income"`, `"asset"` indicating financial amount use `size_min` / `size_max`. Defaults `"revenue"`. underlying columns stored upstream character; function casts numeric inside predicate filter pushes Arrow. size_min, size_max Numeric. Optional inclusive bounds `size_metric` amount. `NULL` (default) leaves side unbounded. Rows `NA` chosen metric dropped either bound set. min_last_year Integer. set, restricts results EINs whose `last_year_in_bmf` (calendar year recent BMF vintage EIN appeared) least value. Use recency / "still active" filter — e.g., `min_last_year = 2024` keeps organizations seen BMF 2024 later. cache Controls local caching master parquet. S3 file hundreds MB; without caching call re-downloads . `TRUE` (default) caches `tools::R_user_dir("nccsdata", "cache")`. character path uses directory instead. `FALSE` skips cache reads directly S3 every call. See [nccs_cache_dir()] [nccs_cache_clear()]. cache_max_age Integer. Maximum age days cached parquet considered stale re-downloaded. Defaults 30 (master rebuilt monthly upstream). Ignored `cache = FALSE`. coerce Logical. `TRUE` (default), known character-typed financial, date, indicator columns coerced natural R types collection (see "Column coercion" ). Set `FALSE` leave every column published upstream. takes effect `collect = TRUE`; `collect = FALSE` lazy Arrow query returned untouched. columns Column selection. `NULL` (default) returns sensible default subset. character vector returns specific columns. `""` returns columns (warning: 400+ MB). Columns used active filters always included. collect Logical. `TRUE` (default), collects result tibble. `FALSE`, returns lazy Arrow query dplyr operations.

title: Read NCCS BMF Data from S3 — nccs_read
text: tibble (`collect = TRUE`) Arrow Dataset query (  `collect = FALSE`).

title: Read NCCS BMF Data from S3 — nccs_read
text: Reads rolling "master" geocoded BMF `s3://nccsdata/geocoding/bmf-master/merged/bmf_master_geocoded.parquet`. specific dated monthly snapshot, see [nccs_vintage_url()] — artifacts CSVs per-vintage schemas exposed function.

title: Read NCCS BMF Data from S3 — nccs_read
text: upstream BMF parquet stores columns `character` design (vintage-stacking requires ). `coerce = TRUE`, `nccs_read()` casts following collected tibble: Numeric: `asset_amount`, `income_amount`, `revenue_amount`,     `geo_score`, `geo_distance`. Date (`YYYY-MM-DD`): `ruling_date`, `tax_period_ymd`. Logical indicators (via [nccs_as_indicator()] `yn`     scheme): `group_exemption_is_member`, `org_addr_is_po_box`,     `org_addr_is_rural_route`, `org_addr_has_special_chars`,     `org_addr_is_missing`, `org_addr_missing_number`,     `org_addr_state_invalid`, `ruling_date_is_missing`,     `tax_period_is_missing`, `in_care_of_name_provided`. Code-like columns (e.g. `subsection_code`, `classification_code`, ZIPs) intentionally left `character` — identifiers, numbers. Columns result (`columns` selection) silently skipped.

title: Read NCCS BMF Data from S3 — nccs_read
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ # All Pennsylvania nonprofits pa <- nccs_read(state = "PA")  # Universities in PA seen in BMF in 2024 or later pa_uni <- nccs_read(   state = "PA",   ntee_subsector = "Universities",   min_last_year = 2024 )  # Arts orgs (major group A) with revenue between $1M and $10M arts_mid <- nccs_read(   ntee_major_group = "A",   size_metric = "revenue",   size_min = 1e6,   size_max = 1e7 )  # Only 501(c)(3) private foundations in California ca_pf <- nccs_read(state = "CA", org_type = "private_foundation")  # Lazy query for custom dplyr chains query <- nccs_read(state = "PA", collect = FALSE) result <- query |>   dplyr::filter(geo_county == "Lackawanna County") |>   dplyr::collect() } # }

what: Read NCCS CORE Series Partitions — nccs_read_core
title: Read NCCS CORE Series Partitions — nccs_read_core
text: Reads one `(tier, tax_year, form)` Form 990 partitions parquet, optional column projection, dplyr-style filtering, local caching. Pass vector years `tax_year` read multiple partitions single query (e.g. `tax_year = 2015:2022`); partitions stacked one Arrow dataset filters column projection push across .

title: Read NCCS CORE Series Partitions — nccs_read_core
code: nccs_read_core(   tier = c("merged", "soi", "legacy"),   tax_year,   form,   columns = NULL,   cache = TRUE,   cache_max_age = 30L,   collect = TRUE,   confirm = interactive() )

title: Read NCCS CORE Series Partitions — nccs_read_core
text: tier One `"merged"` (default, canonical), `"soi"`, `"legacy"`. See Description. tax_year Integer tax year, integer vector years multi-partition read. form Character form code: `"990"`, `"990ez"`, `"990pf"`, `"990combined"`. every form exists every tier — see Description. columns Optional character vector column names project. `NULL` (default) returns columns. Parquet projection means unselected columns never read disk wire. Use [nccs_core_columns()] see available partition. cache Local cache controls. `TRUE` (default) caches parquet [nccs_cache_dir()] `core/<tier>/<tax_year>/<form>/` subdir. character path uses directory instead. `FALSE` reads directly S3 (slower repeat calls, lower disk usage). cache_max_age Integer. Maximum age days cached parquet considered stale re-downloaded. Defaults 30. Ignored `cache = FALSE`. collect Logical. `TRUE` (default) returns tibble. `FALSE` returns lazy Arrow query dplyr operations final `dplyr::collect()`. confirm Logical. `TRUE` multi-partition download required, prompt confirmation reporting total size. Defaults `interactive()` scripts tests proceed silently interactive sessions get guardrail.

title: Read NCCS CORE Series Partitions — nccs_read_core
text: tibble (`collect = TRUE`) Arrow Dataset query   (`collect = FALSE`).

title: Read NCCS CORE Series Partitions — nccs_read_core
text: One row per filing (per `(ein, tax_period)` deduplicated `"merged"` tier). request download multiple partitions, function reports total transfer size (summed partitions already cached) , `confirm = TRUE`, prompts downloading. Partitions published requested tier (e.g. SOI `990pf` 2017-2019) dropped `message()` rather raising error, year range straddles gap still works. See [nccs_core_url()] canonical URL pattern description tier's coverage caveats (especially `"merged"` tier's deduplication missing 2017-2019 `990pf` partitions).

title: Read NCCS CORE Series Partitions — nccs_read_core
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ # One partition, a handful of columns df <- nccs_read_core(   tier = "merged",   tax_year = 2020,   form = "990combined",   columns = c("ein", "tax_period", "total_revenue", "total_expenses") )  # Multi-year: any partition that turns out to be unpublished # upstream is dropped with a message rather than erroring. panel <- nccs_read_core(   tier     = "soi",   tax_year = 2015:2022,   form     = "990pf",   columns  = c("ein", "tax_period", "total_revenue") )  # Lazy query, custom filter, then collect nccs_read_core("merged", 2018:2022, "990combined", collect = FALSE) |>   dplyr::filter(subsection_cd == 3) |>   dplyr::select(ein, tax_period, total_revenue) |>   dplyr::collect() } # }

what: S3 URL of a Historical BMF Vintage — nccs_vintage_url
title: S3 URL of a Historical BMF Vintage — nccs_vintage_url
text: Returns S3 URI specific dated monthly BMF snapshot per-vintage data dictionary. artifacts CSVs per-vintage schemas (central crosswalk) ** geocoded — carry raw Form 990 address columns instead master's `geo_*` columns. Use helper fetch URI, read file `arrow::read_csv_arrow()` `utils::read.csv()`.

title: S3 URL of a Historical BMF Vintage — nccs_vintage_url
code: nccs_vintage_url(vintage, kind = c("data", "dictionary"), legacy = FALSE)

title: S3 URL of a Historical BMF Vintage — nccs_vintage_url
text: vintage Character string form `"YYYY_MM"` (e.g., `"2023_07"`). kind One `"data"` (default) BMF snapshot CSV `"dictionary"` column data dictionary CSV. legacy Logical. `TRUE`, returns legacy-archive path used older vintages (`processed/bmf-legacy/...`). Defaults `FALSE` (modern `processed/bmf/...` path).

title: S3 URL of a Historical BMF Vintage — nccs_vintage_url
text: single character string `s3://` URI.

title: S3 URL of a Historical BMF Vintage — nccs_vintage_url
text: analyses require specific vintage, prefer [nccs_read()], reads rolling geocoded master parquet Arrow predicate-pushdown filters.

title: S3 URL of a Historical BMF Vintage — nccs_vintage_url
code: nccs_vintage_url("2023_07") #> [1] "s3://nccsdata/processed/bmf/2023_07/bmf_2023_07_processed.csv" nccs_vintage_url("2023_09", kind = "dictionary") #> [1] "s3://nccsdata/processed/bmf/2023_09/bmf_2023_09_data_dictionary.csv" nccs_vintage_url("1999_12", legacy = TRUE) #> [1] "s3://nccsdata/processed/bmf-legacy/1999_12/bmf_legacy_1999_12_processed.csv"  if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ # Read a vintage snapshot directly. Schemas differ across vintages # and across the legacy/modern seam — inspect the matching data # dictionary before filtering or joining. uri <- nccs_vintage_url("2023_07") bmf_2023_07 <- arrow::read_csv_arrow(uri) } # }
